#3771. Clair Obscur's narrative lead has left developer Sandfall Interactive after "wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition"

Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year. In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty big bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

"No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.

"One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors."

Her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations."

"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry."

Sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste", and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV shows and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

We know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise, and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

A new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is here, and there's a pretty stellar joke about how much Marvel has changed since the last proper Avengers movie.

The new clip sees the Avengers, the Fantastic Four, and the X-Men all team up to take on a slew of Sentinels. Thor, who has taken on the role of leader, says to them, "I don't even know what half of you do, I don't even know who half of you are..." It's pretty relatable for the casual viewer: so much has changed since Avengers: Endgame hit theaters in 2019.

We didn't even have a proper introduction to the multiverse yet, though we kind of knew what an incursion was (thanks to Kang in Loki season 1). So, Thor trying to grasp who Shang-Chi, the Thunderbolts (aka the New Avengers), Kate Bishop, the Wakandans, and all of the pre-MCU Fox-owned X-Men are is pretty funny.

Me, personally? I can't believe they're going to let Steve Rogers wield Mjölnir for the entire movie.

The epic team-up sees more than 30 heroes band together in order to defeat Doctor Doom. Hailee Steinfeld surprise-announced her involvement in the film (though will she be referred to as Hawkeye... or just Kate Bishop?) less than 24 hours before the trailer dropped, and we can definitely expect to see even more previously unannounced heroes in the upcoming film.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in US theaters on December 18 and a few days earlier in the UK on December 16. For more on the MCU, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#3769. Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang offers to return if that's best for the company and America, Nvidia board essentially say 'nah, we're all good'

New rulers impervious to highly persuasive message of 'come on, please give me my job back, go USA'

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

That last bit seems likely to have been said with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO."

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the company's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

#3768. Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - founded by ex-GTA veteran - has a mountain of debt, and the main plan for paying it back is litigation

"A coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary."

Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the company created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt. And a huge chunk of that appears to be owed to Chinese gaming company NetEase (£36.5m), though more than £1m appears to be owed to Benzies himself.

This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back. And the company's "largest" potential asset, according to the administrators, is litigation.

"Prior to the Company's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

"The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions."

This tallies with the narrative spun by co-company leader Mark Gerhard as the company waded into deep water. Gerhard blamed "organised espionage and corporate sabotage" for the studio's difficulties as multiple rounds of layoffs shredded Build a Rocket Boy. "People had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product," Gerhard said.

The situation he's referring to is likely the alleged smear campaign made against the game, which Gerhand reportedly claimed in an internal meeting this year was paid for by a "big American company" and then run by a UK company called Ritual Network, which apparently had influencers, journalists and staff at Build a Rocket Boy deliberately sabotage the game's release. That's according to an account of a videoed internal meeting reportedly seen by Insider Gaming earlier this year.

It had nothing to do with the dire state of Mindseye when it launched, then. Eurogamer awarded it one out of five stars, chastising its "ridiculous story, inconsistent writing, poorly designed mission scenarios, and utterly atrocious combat" in our Mindseye review.

Build a Rocket Boy was founded in 2016, and its first game, Everywhere - a sort of online gaming platform - was announced in 2022. It never materialised, but a part of that vision was carved out to become a standalone game experience of its own along the way, and that's how we got Mindseye - a take on a Grand Theft Auto formula. Whether or not the litigation is successful and can recoup any of Build a Rocket Boy's debts remains to be seen, but there's a financial mountain for the studio to climb if it hopes to operate again.

Despite this, Howard Scott Warshaw thinks AI will be a "super positive thing" for the industry.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The emergence of generative AI coding tools has numerous effects on the games industry this year, but the prominent of these is that it's made Steam an absolute nightmare to navigate. Since the summer, Steam (and other storefronts like itch.io) have been inundated with clones and AI slop games, as AI users turn to tools like Claude to output thousands of low-quality titles.

For many of us, this seems like a new problem. But for one veteran game developer, the scenario is all too familiar. Howard Scott Warshaw is the developer of numerous Atari 2600 games including Yars' Revenge and Raiders of the Lost Ark. But perhaps his most famous (or infamous) game is 1982's E.T. the Extra Terrestrial, the notorious tie-in game that was so terrible Atari buried unsold copies of it in the desert.

E.T. has been cited as a contributing factor in the US video game industry crash of 1983—one of many poor-quality 8-bit titles that hollowed out the gaming market in the States. It's here where Warshaw sees a parallel to today's emerging scenario, though he doesn't necessarily believe it will end in the same way.

In a talk he gave at the DevGAMM Lisbon conference last week (via GamesIndustry.biz) Warshaw remarked upon how AI coding tools have seemed to rapidly sped up iteration times on game development. "People who used to spend weeks, months or years programming something can now do it in days with AI support," he explained.

"So what does this mean in game development? What it means is we're going to see a lot more games produced. You ever hear of the crash of '83 or '84, the big video game crash? They said the problem that happened in the crash, and I think that was true, was there was a glut of crap on the market, because the machine opened up and anybody could just pop a game out, and they did."

Warshaw pointed out that, at the time "good games were still being made" but these games were "way overshadowed by the crap: and that created a real problem in the game industry." He sees a similar situation emerging now thanks to generative AI tools. "AI is going to have the same impact on a larger scale, because on one level, so many more people can now realise and create a video game than ever could before just using AI. And that's okay, but there's going to be a lot of crap, because most games suck. That's just the way it is."

The reason for this, Warshaw says, is that, like all artistic endeavours "there's some things in life that everybody can see themselves doing, and the truth is most people who do it can't do it very well. And what AI is going to do is make that more possible for people who can't do it to do it." Yet while he thinks that most of the games that result from these ideas "aren't going to be very interesting" he also believes that "it's also going to enable the people who really do have some innovative, interesting and solid ideas to realise those, too."

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

In short, Warshaw believes that AI will provoke a shift away from technology development to a greater focus on game design, which he ultimately believes is "actually going to be a super positive thing for the video game industry." He also said that, despite observing similar warning signs as in 1983, he doesn't "see the prospect of a crash in the video game industry" and instead expects to see a "reorganisation, where we need better filters to figure out a way to get rid of the garbage games".

Warshaw is certainly correct about AI tools resulting in a flood of crap, but I also think he himself overvalues the inherent worth of ideas in terms of what makes a great game. While ideas themselves can be inherently good or bad, no idea emerges from the creative process unscathed. Indeed, a major factor in creating art of any kind is engaging and grappling with that process, learning how to deal with the friction between the image in your head and what ends up on the page, or the canvas, or your scripting program. That mastery only comes through practice and experience. It cannot be outsourced or circumvented.

But that doesn't change the fact that storefronts are currently being overwhelmed with terrible, AI-assisted games, and it's having all manner of knock-on effects. Earlier this month, Valve admitted it is "running behind" on approving Steam games because it has to keep re-reviewing them, and although Valve didn't cite AI as the cause of this, it's an awful coincidence that this has started happening as AI coding tools result in game submissions shooting through the roof.

#3765. Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

Administrators say "a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise"

Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Announced in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

The same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The company grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "currently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

This is the cheapest Alienware laptop in Dell's sales

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The big question going into Black Friday this year is how far the RAM crisis will affect the deals. Dell's response to this is to ask "what crisis?" as it's launched its own Black Friday deals on a range of its Alienware products, and there are some pretty massive discounts on gaming laptops.

Any purchase on Dell's Black Friday site gets you a range of bonuses, but they stack best with a deal cutting $900 off the Alienware 16 Aurora, on certain configurations. This lets you pick up a laptop with a great-looking display, Intel Core processor and specs designed for mid-range gaming, all at a bargain price.

The Alienware 16 Aurora with an RTX 5050, 16GB memory and 512GB storage is best discounted, with $900 off. Models with a better graphics card, more memory or extra storage are also discounted to varying degrees, but this reduction saves the most money.

With any purchase from Dell's website over Black Friday, you get certain perks. The brand's offering 30% off software tools like McAfee or Microsoft 365, as well as a multi-buy discount on years of its Alienware Elite Care support service. The best deal, though, is that you get 25 free Xbox games; the brand hasn't listed what they are, but says they have a $500 value.

The version of Alienware 16 Aurora with the biggest discount, listed above, is also the weakest. Its Nvidia GeForce RTX 5050 is the lowest-end member of the brand's most recent graphics card line-up, and the 16GB RAM isn't enough for the most advanced games either.

So this laptop is best for mid-range or low-end games, whether that's new indie titles, older games or the big names of yesteryear at their lowest graphics options. That's not to criticize the laptop, and many people won't need anything stronger than that.

The Alienware 16 Aurora also comes in models with the 4050, 5060 and 5070, and there are discounts on at least one version with each, but the savings aren't as good.

We've reviewed the Alienware 16X Aurora laptop, which is a more advanced model than the one listed above, but with a much higher price.

Several 16X Aurora models are discounted by up to $400, but given that it's already a more expensive option than the 16, that means the deal prices are at least $1,000 more than the reduced 16.

If you've got the budget for the Alienware 16X Aurora, you'll notice the difference when you're playing games, so it might seem like a better buy. But that price is a lot higher.

It's worth asking if you need this high-spec laptop. If you don't plan to play any GPU-intensive games, an RTX 5050 might be enough. And if you want a little more power, it may be more economical to find a more powerful 16 Aurora, rather than add the 'X'.

#3763. Infinity Nikki fans threaten to boycott game after promotion by Elon Musk's mother, but there may be a genuine reason for her involvement

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates. Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother.

Some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a new update - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car", which doesn't actually fly.

While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.

"If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear."

"If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread. "Please please please be wrong."

Though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained.

"She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY."

Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content".

"A Chinese company makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added.

So far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players.

In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review, Jessica Orr said it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020."

#3762. PC remains GTA 6's last hope for 60fps smoothness as Rockstar confirm such an option isn't coming to even the swankiest consoles

Poor little game boxes just can't handle it

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates."

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood.

I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN, Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom.

"A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer."

Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there."

While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. But it's such commitment to representing its world that has led GTA 6 to receive near-universal praise from critics, and it probably didn't hurt when it earned $3.79 billion on launch day, either.

Find a serial killer in GTA 6 when you locate three missing tourists in Port Gellhorn

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There's a GTA 6 serial killer to find once you reach Chapter 2. You may have noticed three missing person posters in the Starlet Motel reception - three Port Gellhorn tourists went missing over 20 years ago, yet no one has been able to locate them. However, the posters include a tip line number you can ring, should you happen to find the missing people. This GTA 6 side mission is easy to miss, but finding all three missing tourists leads you to a deranged serial killer – a bit like in the Red Dead Redemption 2 Killer Clue mystery. However, whether you decide to hunt down the killer alone or with your partner has consequences on how this mission plays out.

The Missing Person GTA 6 mission can be started in GTA 6 Chapter 2 as Lucia (or as Jason once you unlock the ability to switch characters in GTA 6). To start this GTA 6 mission go to the bunker-like warehouse slightly north-east of Moses' garage in Port Gellhorn. It's a long dome building covered in overgrown foliage and graffiti with a shutter on its front – you can see it if you look right from the front of Moses' garage. If you try to break in through the shutter, the shutter immediately drops as soon as you try to lift it. Instead, go to the north-east side of the building and you'll find a space you can crawl through to get in.

Once inside, turn left and walk straight, then enter the small room with the red light on your right. Go through this room and into the next one; it appears to be a trophy room, inside which you'll find two missing posters on the right-hand wall and an armchair facing a row of lockers. Each locker contains creepy framed photographs of the missing tourists from the posters and what appears to be their belongings. Examine each of the three sets of photographs carefully as the images hint where you'll find that missing person.

Below, I've broken down where you can find each of the three missing people in GTA 6, with a more detailed breakdown available in the sections which follow.

Susanne Keeble's photographs are found in the first locker in the creepy building's trophy room. The first photo appears to show her pink car outside a junkyard and the second shows a close off of her car, which has the license plate "PRTTYGRL."

Head to the Port Gellhorn Pay 'N' Spray and go behind the garage to find the junk yard (slightly south-east). At the junkyard's entrance, look left to see a "No Parking" sign, and you should spot Susanne's pink car behind it. Jump the fence and press Y/Triangle to open the trunk. You'll find Susanne's remains inside. Select Y/Triangle to report the body to the Kelly County Missing Persons Tip Line.

Patrick Murray's locker is the second one (from the left) in the trophy room. His photographs show a trailer in the shadow of a water tower and a newspaper clipping. The water tower is in north-east Port Gellhorn, so head toward there and you should see the tower's orb-shaped structure in the distance.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Once you arrive at the water tower, jump the fence north of it to enter a trailer park that's in its shadow – like in the photograph. Enter the accessible trailer that's closest to the tower/fence you jumped (a dog barks at the door). When you enter the trailer look at the gap in the floorboards to your right, then select Triangle/Y to examine the floorboards. Your character will lift the floorboards to find Patrick Murray's remains under the floor. Select Triangle/Y to report the body to Kelly County TIp Line, but this time, someone will answer your call.

The third and final locker contains photographs of Donald Miller, with the images taken at a lake near a snarled tree. The lake in the images is the one that is shaped like a U with a tail, right on the border between Port Gellhorn and Wild Hog Point, southwest of Port Gellhorn, just before the bridge.

Look for the tree and you'll find a submerged car next to the tree stump near it. Wade into the water and then press Y/Triangle when prompted to examine the car, revealing Donald Miller's remains in the passenger seat. Once again, press Triangle/Y on your controller to report the body.

After finding the final body, you need to wait until the Kelly County TIp Line contact calls you. This can take some time and I didn't receive a call until night, after unlocking Jason as a playable character again by completing the Chapter 2 Breakfast Run mission. It appears you need access to both characters before you can progress this GTA 6 side mission.

When the TIp Line contact does call, he'll tell you that he's looked into the evidence you've collected and he thinks there's another victim. He asks you to meet him back at warehouse where you found the lockers (officially called the creepy building) to discuss his findings.

How the rest of this mission plays out depends on whether you meet the contact alone or as a pair. If you go to the warehouse as a couple, completing the Missing Person mission is easier, but completing it alone is more exciting and offers the opportunity to increase your GTA 6 relationship status. Stop reading here if you want to avoid spoilers.

Head back to the creepy building in Port Gellhorn as either Jason or Lucia. Once again, crawl through the gap in the wall and follow the stranger's calls into the trophy room. When you enter the room, you'll meet the ominous Alvan West, who points you toward the end locker, where you find a photograph of Jason and Lucia. Immediately Alvan attacks you, holding a chloroform cloth to your nose and mouth. Regardless of whether you successfully struggle or not, Alvan will kidnap you.

You then switch to your partner, who receives a suspicious message asking you to meet them at an abandoned mine near the Kalaga Reservoir in Lummox County's Mount Kalaga National Park. When you arrive at the waypoint, enter the abandoned mine and follow the green lights to find your partner trapped in a wooden box weighed down with rocks. After freeing them, don't simply follow the green lights to find Alvan, but use focus mode to follow his voice (struggling against him when he ambushes you).

You eventually fall out of a tunnel and Alvan ambushes you again. Fend him off and then chase him to the dead end that sits over a huge drop. Alvan begins begging for his life, but you must not listen to his pleas. If you don't shoot him immediately he grabs a pickaxe from behind a crate and whacks you in the stomach, killing you instantly. The only option you have is to kill Alvan. His body will fall off the wooden ledge and into the darkness below.

With Alvan dead, return to your partner and you'll head back to the motel. Whoever was kidnapped will not immediately be available to switch to, but if you ask them to team up and both head outside, you can then switch back to them. While you don't get a monetary reward for completing this side mission, it does improve Jason and Lucia's relationship status.

Make sure you have grouped up Jason and Lucia then use the crawl space to enter the creepy building again. Go to the trophy room and you'll meet Alvan. Rather than one of you being kidnapped, Jason and Lucia confront Alvan about his crimes.

#3757. Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

It "ticks many of the boxes", despite the funding problems

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the new team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

#3756. You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

You cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5, but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title.

You can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a new manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a big heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting.

It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," says David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style."

That means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," says Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply.

In the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear.

GTA 6 comes out tomorrow. You can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 at the link, and read our 5-star review of the game here. If you want to, ahem, 'travel to New Zealand' to get ahead of the timezones, it seems the country would be happy to have you.

You'll have to track down the GTA 6 Riata locations to fix the second Classic Car Collection vehicle for Wyman. He'll text you a little while after you complete the Transgressor, this time sending you to the Key Lento area, unfortunately a rather long drive when you're likely still at the motel near Port Gellhorn.

There are three Riatas you need to scan with the WAiNK It app to fix up this classic off-roading 4x4, one in Key Lento itself, one near the naval base at Goose Key, and a final one in Shoeless Keys.

This is the first one Wyman asks you to find, near the PD in the Keys. It's under a brown stilt house north of Leonida Key Lento Mini-mart and the Shrimp 'n Save, on that northernmost road running through the Key. Find the brown stilt house, as in the video above, then just head underneath to scan the car.

This second one is located in Southwind, on Goose Key, the island with the Mile Zero Air Station to the west of Key Lento—you will have visited here for a mission early in the game. The junked car is under another brown stilt house at the end of the road down to the east from the Xero Gas - Southwind station, on the right just before the sea.

This third one is located behind the ruined gas station just to the north of Grassrivers Cafe & Deli in Shoeless Keys. The tricky part is that this is a four-star area (because of the final missions in Chapter 1), so you'll want to be quick as otherwise a police chopper will come and spot you. When you turn off the main road, the garage is on your left before you reach the cafe itself, with the car just behind.

Somehow, I forgot to record this one, but I still show the location in the clip above behind the gas station (just without the car since it was gone when I re-recorded).

Once you have all three, Wyman will tell you to wait a little while, and then will call and ask you to Buck him $1,500 for the labour. Select the payment request in the text, or do it manually in the app. A little while after the money is sent, you'll get a map marker for Wyman's scrapyard, where you can pick up this completed classic car.

#3754. SteamDB will add "affiliate links to authorised game retailers" and a new tab dedicated to mods, first update since Nexus Mods takeover confirms

"We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve"

In a first substantial update since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick update on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

There are two main new features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that shows off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

"We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you."

That seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

"We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region."

Folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

Beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how quickly the team can react to issues have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively new custodians of both it and SteamDB.

GTA 6 is finally here a good 13 years after Grand Theft Auto 5, bringing a unique male and female duo of protagonists for players to choose from with it: Lucia and Jason.

The couple certainly stands out when put beside past games' own leads, especially seeing as it shines the spotlight on a woman (yes, very old entries like the original Grand Theft Auto let you choose between female characters, too, but newer games like Rockstar's fifth have not) – and former developers like Brian Baglow, who worked on the OG GTA, think it's a breath of fresh air compared to the usual male formula.

Regarding the franchise's portrayal of women, Baglow tells CBC that the representation "has not been good, to put it mildly." That checks out, considering all the backlash entries as recent as GTA 5 spurred by instances of sexism and questionable themes. "I'm delighted that we now have not only a female protagonist, but a Hispanic female protagonist," he adds. "I think it's been long, long overdue."

The ex-Rockstar dev says it's a sign of improvement on the studio's part: "I think it's showing a level of maturation because from the very earliest days it was a very young group of almost entirely male developers in Scotland." And, back to the controversy past entries sparked for their representation of women (or lack thereof), like GTA 5 – Baglow describes how it's not likely the company didn't take any note of that.

"I don't think that could have passed Rockstar by, so I'm relatively sure Lucia would have been part of their plans from quite early on," he concludes. I suppose that makes sense. After all, it's been well over a decade now since Grand Theft Auto 5, giving the team plenty of time to address any long-standing feedback from fans and critics alike. The topic of women in the franchise would offer no exception there.

#3752. Just how detailed is the audio in GTA 6? Well, even convenience store refrigerators "all have their own unique sounds", says Rockstar dev

If you've been online at all today, you'll know that what feels like the entire world is currently fawning over GTA 6. As the reviews dropped, one thing quickly became very clear: this is a game absolutely packed with detail. Our own Chris noted that, thanks to this focus on specific detail and unbelievable nuance, Grand Theft Auto 6 is "the most unbelievable video game world ever made". And it's no accident: this is something Rockstar put a lot of dedicated effort into.

It's been well-established that the studio has gone above and beyond to make this interactive world one of the most richly-developed we've ever seen: Rockstar has told us it "re-engineered" its weather systems to "achieve a sense of scale we haven't felt before," adding hurricanes, rainbows and heavy rain. It simulated and built a complex drug system, allowing Lucia and Jason to partake in drug use "directly from their inventory" and "at any time". But there are still details emerging from the dev team that are blowing my mind. And the most recent byte of information I saw was related to how Rockstar worked with sound.

"Much of the dynamic soundscape is informed by the incredibly detailed art throughout the world," explains Alastair MacGregor, vice president of audio at Rockstar. "One small example is that convenience store refrigerators all have their own unique sounds. In a run-down store, the refrigerators and freezers are loud and sound like they are badly maintained. Their compressor units can be heard mechanically whirring away from years of neglect. As a result, the bottles behind the doors can be heard shaking and the units click on and off more frequently. In an up-market store, the refrigerators are quieter, adding a subtle hum to the environment."

This level of detail is, quite frankly, absurd. It's a testament to granularity Rockstar is willing to go to in making Leonida feel truly lived-in and realistic. And this level of production isn't restricted to internal locations, either. "On the ambient side, we love the contrast between the manicured luxury islands, with the sizzle of crickets and lawn sprinklers backed by birdsong, yacht halyards clanging in the distance, and yard work going on, versus urban areas with the sounds of people living on top of each other - snatches of every genre of music, distant voices, cars peeling out, construction, the omnipresent hum of elderly air conditioners struggling with the humidity," continues MacGregor.

He goes on to say that if you're wandering the streets of Gellhorn - a coastal city in Kelly County on the western side of Leonida - it's acoustically a very different vibe than the high-rise centre of Vice City, where the sound bounces between the buildings. This means that the engine is handling not just the sounds of things as minute as bugs in the grass, but also how that sound travels, and interacts with other physical entities in the world. "We've spent years iterating on reverb technology to make sure that you can feel that - from the pops of cars backfiring to the wash of a helicopter passing by overhead to birds squawking in the trees," concludes MacGregor.

GTA 6 launches tomorrow - Thursday, 19th November - for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It's also worth noting that Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

#3751. "It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 launches on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off

Even though they've "had no indication that layoffs are coming" from bosses

GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.

In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

The animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section. Following some personal reflections on his time at the studio, he calls on other Rockstar devs to get behind the union, describing it as both "a huge step forward" for a company that has previously faced allegations of "crunch culture", and a win for UK game developers at large. "What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more," Uriarte writes.

The vote at Rockstar North will run till 26th November, and could give rise to a union spanning over 1600 developers, according to umbrella organisation the Independent Workers of Great Britain. If that comes to pass, it would make the Rockstar union the largest recognised videogame developer union in the UK.

It comes as the company and a group of fired workers await the result of an employment tribunal battle over alleged "union-busting". Rockstar has accused the workers in question of "gross misconduct" and a breach of confidentiality by means of a union Discord server. Amongst other things, the legal brawl has revealed that Rockstar had a mole on that server for two and a half years, prior to the firings.

As for the prospect of further job losses, after GTA 6 goes on sale, Uriarte cites a wave of mass layoffs across the industry that has affected the creators of even commercially successful games like Battlefield 6 and Netflix's FIFA World Cup.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," he writes. "Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

The obvious context here is that GTA 6 has been a massively expensive production, with a development team headcount in the thousands. While one could accuse Uriarte of fear-mongering, I do find it hard to believe that executives at parent company Take-Two aren't weighing up some timely "down-sizing" right now. In general, videogame companies have a long tradition of axing the books once a game has been shipped, despite arguments that keeping experienced teams intact often pays off. In Rockstar's case, however, it's also worth bearing in mind that the GTA 6 rolling out this week is only part of the package. There's also the hazy prospect of the next incarnation of GTA Online, which – going by GTA 5 sales – will be a money spinner for many years, and will require a sizeable staff to maintain. Oh, and of course there's the PC version.

Echoing many peers, Uriarte also argues in his piece that it's important to unionise now in order to negotiate proper protection against generative AI cost-cutting initiatives. "The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry," he continues. "Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI.

"Rockstar has said it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people," Urirarte concedes. "But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together."

#3750. 1666: Amsterdam Early Access first major update launches in December

Panache Digital Games will release the first major content update for the Early Access version of dark third-person narrative action adventure game 1666: Amsterdam in December, the developer announced. It will expand the game’s world, story, and supernatural abilities.

The December update marks the first major expansion of the Early Access experience, bringing new areas to explore, new supernatural abilities, and another Original for players to confront.

A New Region, a New Original, and More Witchcraft

Arriving during the final moon of the year, the first major update marks the beginning of a series of planned expansions for 1666: Amsterdam.

Players will be able to explore Ouderkerk, a new region slightly larger than the game’s currently available area, effectively doubling the world players can explore. Alongside this new location comes another Esbat and a new Original, bringing the next chapter of Noa’s journey to Early Access.

The update will also introduce additional Lux and Nux spells and combos, along with new jewels and potions, giving players more ways to develop their abilities and approach encounters.

Panache Digital Games will share more details about these additions in the weeks leading up to the December release.

Panache Digital Games has also confirmed that 1666: Amsterdam will remain at its current Early Access price when the December update launches, with no price increase for the new content.

This first major update is part of the team’s ongoing Early Access roadmap, with further expansions planned as development continues.

1666: Amsterdam is available now in Early Access for PC via Steam and Epic Games Store.

Tracking down the GTA 6 Mamba GT locations is how you restore the third classic car Wyman asks you to help with. After completing the Transgressor and then the Riata, he'll send you a text with details about fixing this classic 60s roadster.

There are four Mambas to scan with the WAiNK It app in the counties around Port Gellhorn, so this one is a little more involved than the previous cars.

The first Mamba GT is in the garage of a farmhouse to the north of Leonida State Prison, which is southeast of Gellhorn. Head north up the main road to the east of the prison until you spot a private property gate on the left side of the road, opposite a building on the other side with Gruppe6 written on it.

Smash the gate and head up the track to the house where you'll find the wreck in the garage to the left of it (you can enter via the backdoor). There's also a little cash in a box here, too.

The second wrecked car is in the town of Ambrosia, east of Port Gellhorn, near the Xero Gas - Ambrosia station and the purchasable Wyatt Motors garage. Head right down the side of the gas station, turn right into the alley, and continue a little way until you spot a white garage door to your right, next to a big blue garage door. Interact to open the white one and find your Mamba GT to scan.

The third Mamba GT is sunk in a pool at the Thrillbilly Mud Club—you will have visited here in the story with Wyman, when you met Billy and had a race, east of Port Gellhorn in Frogswater. Travel to the Mud Club - Dirt Track Races nav point, then head to the small pool just east of it to find the car partially submerged but still scannable from the shore.

This last one is by far the hardest to get to. It's located on the north coast of Leonida in Lummox County, in the wreckage of a collapsed wooden bridge, to the east along the coast from the little town of Bonanza. It's also northwest of the Buck Creek Country Store.

Chances are, you won't have been to this area yet, but you can just set a nav marker in Moreau or Bonanza on the map and then work it out when you get there. The broken bridge is easy to spot since it's on the northernmost coastal road. Drop down to the ravine below the bridge to scan the car in the wreckage.

As with the previous cars, once you've found all four, Wyman will take a little time and then call asking you to Buck him $1,500 for his labor. Accept the payment request in the text or do it manually, after which a nav marker will appear to collect the Mamba GT from his scrapyard, same as with the other cars.

#3748. I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

Almost nothing here works, figuratively and literally. Within three minutes of the opening mission, before Madsen's undercover cop Tanner goes undercover, you're ordered to join some marked police cars to head for a bust – but because the rozzers' primary function is to give chase to you, later on, driving too close crosses their wires, provoking them into blue-on-blue ramming maneuvres. Later, in a motorbike sprint down an inexplicably exploding beach, cartel goons are positioned across the sand, presumably to take drama-enhancing pot shots. They're so slow, however, both to notice your presence and to physically raise their guns, that they're barely out of their idle animations by the time you whizz past. And your own guy isn't much better: an assassination mission, which ends with your target cornered from an elevated position, requires that you take a few steps backwards first, as Tanner can't drop his shootin' arms low enough to land a hit from the balcony he's on.

Unlike Vice City's Tommy Vercetti, he can at least swim, which by 2004 standards gives the seaside Miami and Nice maps a fair verisimilitude, particularly when a shot-up boat engine forces the abandoning of ship. No amount of product-of-its-time concessions, though, can account for how woodenly unpalatable the on-foot action is. Controls are stiff and shooting feels meaningless, with zero tangible sense of bullets being sent nor received; killing a man carries all the weight of just shouting at him to lie down, and if it weren't for sound effects and the dwindling health bar, I could park Tanner in front of a firing squad of identically-modelled thugs with almost zero impression that his lungs were filling with Uzi rounds.

Driver, of course, began as a pure wheelman sim, later installments only letting you hoof it after someone at developers Reflections began smelling that Rockstar money. It was therefore always unlikely, even for the purported GTA killer, that this would achieve action-adventure sophistication in its bipedal bits. Even so, god, it's woeful. Stingy checkpointing also means that failure is often punished by having to replay those tedious, flavourless shootouts in full.

The driving is better, which is a bit like saying there's decent cheese in this cheese and smallpox toastie. It's reasonably slidey, when throwing the back end through a curving French alleyway, and in contrast to the gunplay, there is a somewhat realised tactility to ploughing around in two tonnes of rolling metal. It has problems of its own, mind. Cars feel okay when they're moving, but contact and crashes are leaden, sluggish, visually underwhelming occasions that I would call non-events, were they not so slow to recover from that a single nasty impact can scupper a timed mission. Granted, I quickly re-learned how vital it is to keep both eyes on the road, as other vehicles, pedestrians, lamposts, and other detritus tend to pop into existence some mere fifty feet in front of my speeding bumper.

The result, of both this graphical shortcoming and the overly punishing crashes, is a getaway car sim that too often encourages you to drive like cataract-ridden grandparent. Worse, whoever put Letty Ortiz in a lunchbox must have also been in charge of the engine noises, producing an array of miserable high-rev dins – especially for the motorbikes, which screech like amateurishly autotuned vacuum cleaners. There are also shades of that deranged cop AI in ordinary commuters, who I've repeatedly seen swerving and slaloming around empty lanes, seemingly for no reason beyond violent confusion.

Strangely enough, my 2026 return has largely dodged the game's infamous glitchiness, the worst instance of physics defiance being a garage door that appeared to lift Tanner into the air before propelling him, incorporeally, through the car shed's roof. I recall much worse, from the days when I'd have my dad rent it for me from Blockbuster. Mission-critical NPCs getting stuck on walls; flipped pursuit cars spinning endlessly; getting flung into space when walking on an overturned vehicle (a common occurrence, given the actual 'crawling out' animation sometimes failed to play, the game instead teleporting you onto the spring-loaded underside instead).

I've thus far escaped these, but as far as I know, they're still lurking dormant, and none of what I've witnessed with adult eyes has been funny or stupid enough to imbue Driv3r 3 The Third with a Wiseauean so-bad-it's-good quality. It's just bad. It was always bad. Why did I even entertain the possibility that it wasn't bad?

Reflections, to their credit, accepted their folly. Narratively unrelated sequel Driver: Parallel Lines tucked away a bin full of discarded copies, at least until Ubisoft bought up the series and patched it out, and for all the fantastical coma silliness of direct followup Driver: San Francisco, that was sensible enough to keep Tanner where he best belongs: hands on the wheel, foot on the gas, gun holstered. And was a far, far better game for it, too.

As 2011's San Francisco launch also remains the most recent Driver release, I regretfully can't end with the assurance that DrIIIver's legacy is a mere blip on a redeemed franchise. That stain stank, and did for ages, very possibly to the extent that GTA's one-time biggest rival never recovered.

Still, even if Reflections couldn't fully turn around their fortunes, the consistent improvement from this to Parallel Lines to San Francisco showed that they did learn something. Maybe so too did anyone else who went on to make an open-world action game. Which wouldn't be the worst outcome; after all, those who do not learn from gnarled, stinking wrecks like this are doomed to repeat them.

#3746. Arknights: Endfield version update ‘Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms’ launches November 25

Publisher GRYPHLINE and developer Mountain Contour will release the version update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” for free-to-play 3D RPG Arknights: Endfield on November 25, the companies announced. The game’s latest live stream also introduced the upcoming version 2.0 update, which takes players to Gypsosia and aboard the Rhodes Island landship, and teased 10 characters who will join the journey across upcoming content updates.

“With Wuling’s story wrapping up, and the main story taking us through all the heavy moments, we want to give you a change of pace with a lighthearted, upbeat update,” said Arknights: Endfield producer Light Zhong in a press release.

Here is an overview of the update, via GRYPHLINE:

Version Update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms”

Strange mushrooms have overrun an abandoned dam outside Wuling, where Landbreakers worship a giant mushroom and visitors keep slipping into hallucinations. There, the Endministrator meets Kay, a Rhodes Island Operator who has been adventuring alone across Talos-II in search of them. Kay happily shares everything she treasures, including a towering stack of honey waffles. But which would she choose: a mountain of waffles or a dear friend?

A Nature Vanguard with a carefree fighting style, Kay throws weapons that scatter across the battlefield, then gathers them up for a heavy hammer slam. Along the way, she drops Picnic Snacks that heal her teammates.

The Old Dam, the update’s new area, has grown into a fairytale-like mushroom kingdom. Players fire Kay’s honey waffles at mushrooms to open doors and spin fungal bridges, and must avoid Loquacious Shrooms that scramble their sense of direction. Mushroom foes like the Bolete Prince guard the dam, and a mushroom as tall as a mountain waits at its heart.

The update’s music leans into its whimsical tone, with Ori composer Gareth Coker and ambient producer Owsey returning to score Kay’s honey waffle adventure. It caps a first year in which the soundtrack has followed the story, from the sweeping sci-fi orchestral sound of Valley IV to the choir-driven battle against Alleikhreos, Typhoeus’s JRPG-inspired winter journey and the modern electronic take on Eastern music in Si’s painted world.

Later in the update, every player who logs in during the Workers’ Guards: Roll Call event will receive the Operator Mimino and her signature weapon, Star of Tomorrow, for free, with event missions offering extra copies to reach full Potential. Operators Gilberta and Rossi also return in successive reruns.

For factory builders, Exclusion Zone Rebuilding is a new permanent mode in which players supply materials across four phases to restore the North Wuling Exclusion Zone, using the new Forge of Luminance to transform products on their conveyor belts. For a lighter break, Lucky Carrot’s Games of Wonder adds two multiplayer card games, Witch’s Darkjack and Band Uprising, that players can enjoy with friends or through matchmaking.

A First Look at Version 2.0 and Rhodes Island

The livestream also previewed the next chapter of Arknights: Endfield, arriving in the new year. Exiles have launched attacks across the Civilization Band, and their real target is Rhodes Island. The Endministrator sets out with Perlica into Gypsosia, the Cretaceous Frontiers, where players will be able to board and explore Rhodes Island itself, a massive landship. A 10-character teaser offered a glimpse of companions for the journey, including Warfarin, appearing as the leader of Rhodes Island, and M3, who returns looking completely different.

The chapter’s first update will add four new maps at once, including Rhodes Island. Main Mission Early Unlock: Gypsosia will let players who have completed the main mission Remediation Progress skip ahead to the new story while still earning all beginner-event rewards. New modes are also in development for future updates, including a management sim with the Golden Branch Tribe and the Shattered Protocol combat mode.

Arknights: Endfield is now Steam Deck Verified, with default controller support and every feature available on Valve’s handheld. The update also brings Despot Weaponized, a new high-difficulty challenge series in Umbral Monument; the return of RISE! MEGA ARENA!, a two-Operator arena event; and new seasons of the Echoes of War combat mode.

Arknights: Endfield is available now for PlayStation 5, PC via the official launcher, Steam, and Epic Games Store, iOS via App Store, and Android via Google Play.

#3744. GTA 6 breaks the all-time livestream viewer record hours before it's available to play for most of the world

Hours before it's even playable in most of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken the record for the most viewers across livestreaming platforms like Twitch.

According to streaming data and analytics website Streams Charts, GTA 6 had amassed 6.38m live viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick at 12:30 UTC today. At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in New Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

The previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

Twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 launches officially in more regions of the world.
